chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
The witness is Friday, that which is to be witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and that which is promised is the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الشَّاهِدُ: The witness (referring to Friday as a day of witnessing divine grace)
key_terms.وَالْمَشْهُودُ: And that which is witnessed (referring to the Imam on the Day of Arafah)
key_terms.وَالْمَوْعُودُ: And that which is promised (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of Friday, Arafah, and the Day of Resurrection according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a theological triad linking the weekly, annual, and eschatological realms through the concept of 'witnessing' (shahadah). Friday serves as the microcosmic witness to the Imam's presence and divine grace, while the Day of Arafah represents the annual pilgrimage's climax where the Imam is visibly witnessed by the faithful. This framework underscores the Shia belief that the Imam is the central axis of cosmic order, connecting the believer's weekly devotion to the ultimate Day of Resurrection. Additionally, the term 'al-Maw'ud' (the Promised One/Day) for the Day of Judgment highlights the certainty of divine covenant, a theme deeply rooted in Shia eschatology.
